name: Body makeup / leg makeup

lead: Body makeup, including leg makeup and bronzers, is a wash-off cosmetic that adds colour or evens skin tone, often for photos or events.
It is discussed as a quick alternative or complement to self-tanner. No clinical studies have examined it.

paras: The product deposits a temporary tint on the skin surface and is removed with soap and water.[1]
Reported drawbacks are rub-off onto clothing, uneven or orange-looking results, and possible allergens such as fragrances or benzyl alcohol in some formulations.

lead: Body makeup, often sold as leg makeup, is a cosmetic applied to the skin of the body to even out tone, cover blemishes or add colour for a photo or event. It belongs to the family of temporary tints and bronzers, which wash off with soap and water.[1]

Encyclopedic sources describe bronzers as available in powders, sprays, mousses, gels, lotions and moisturizers, often used for a one-day tan or alongside dihydroxyacetone (DHA) self-tanner. Reported drawbacks include rub-off onto clothing, and an orange or splotchy look if applied unevenly.[1]
No published trials have tested body makeup for appearance outcomes, so its effect rests on the product descriptions and on user experience.

paras: Temporary bronzing and tinting products colour only the surface of the skin and do not involve the chemical reaction that DHA self-tanners use.[1] Some bronzers also contain a gradual tanning agent, so the colour builds with repeated use.[1]
Listed drawbacks include transfer onto clothing and uneven results. Some formulations contain potential allergens such as benzyl alcohol, tocopherol and fragrances.[1]
